evidence: The original header said 'Four scripts here each carried their own copy' as if all were consolidated, while signWebhook and mintToken stayed untouched. The reviewer offered narrowing the comment as one option, and 20172c2 did exactly that, which is a defensible scope call for a diagnosis PR.

evidence: microphone() resolves on room.once(LocalTrackSubscribed), so with two listeners it can resolve on the first. Gating at the one call site with subscribed() avoids a count parameter that every other caller would pass as 1. The five re-runs showed the failures were not caused by harness timing.
guidance_note: When a new caller is the first to use a shared helper in a new topology (two subscribers instead of one), re-read the helper's wait conditions for assumptions about that topology before wiring it in.

evidence: The `* 10` literals re-derive FRAMES_PER_SECOND. 20172c2 exports millis() and replaces all the sites, including the unflagged `AUDIBLE_MS / 10` in live-call-acceptance.mjs.

evidence: This duplicates F1 on the same line and the same overstated 'Four scripts' header, and the single 20172c2 header edit resolves both.

The 'spelled once' docstring overclaimed canonicity over Rust-side grants. But making token-endpoint-acceptance assert against joinToken() would destroy its independence as a contract test, as the agent argued. The docstring fix in 20172c2 states the hand-maintained mirror and the asymmetry.

evidence: `perFrame = sampleRate / FRAMES_PER_SECOND` with a zero rate gives `at += 0`, an infinite loop. 20172c2 refuses non-positive rates in readRecording (the boundary) and in sounding (SFU frames have no parser in front), and labels the inland guard as a named exception.
guidance_note: When a function divides by or steps by an input, check every producer of that input for a zero or degenerate value before shipping it.

evidence: The reviewer inferred DeleteRoom's grant requirement from another script's grant shape and said it could not confirm it. The agent measured CreateRoom 200 and DeleteRoom 200 with only {roomCreate, roomList}, which matches livekit-server authorizing DeleteRoom on create permission.

The narrowing from `?? []` to a destructuring default is real, but the agent measured ListRooms returning `{"rooms":[]}`, so it is unreachable. A null from the SFU would be a protocol violation that a loud TypeError reports better than a silent 0-rooms success.

The wait required `heard.audibleFrames >= published.audibleFrames` while the check accepted 0.9 of that, so healthy runs burned SETTLE_MS and printed 'gave up'. 20172c2 derives one ENOUGH constant used by both. The reply-hint 'pushback' is wrong: the reply opens 'Plan: valid'.
guidance_note: When a wait precedes a check on the same quantity, derive both thresholds from one named constant in the original code.

evidence: The script creates a room and cleaned up only on the happy path. 20172c2 wraps it in try/finally, but leaves CreateRoom and recordSpeech outside the try and DeleteRoom unguarded in finally, which costs F16 and F25 later.
guidance_note: When adding a try/finally for a resource, list every statement between acquisition and the try and every call in the finally that can throw, and resolve each one in the same commit.

evidence: This is the same narrowing as F8. The measured `{"rooms":[]}` makes it unreachable, and restoring `?? []` would turn a protocol violation into a misleading 'room not created' check failure.

With a fractional perFrame (22050 Hz gives 220.5), typed-array indexing returns undefined and NaN poisons the peak. The agent had already committed 5cc868f locally (round the stride) and it landed in 20172c2. The diff shows `Math.round(sampleRate / FRAMES_PER_SECOND)`.
guidance_note: When a stride is computed by division, round it or assert it is an integer at the point it is computed.

evidence: loopback-acceptance's header claims it speaks 'the same recording' as stt-acceptance, but it carried an independent copy of the literal. 20172c2 moves SPOKEN into caller.mjs and both scripts import it.
guidance_note: When a new script's premise is 'identical to X', import X's value rather than copying it.

evidence: 20172c2 added the zero-rate guard in both readRecording and sounding, but its caller.test.mjs additions test only sounding's RangeError. The agent conceded: 'I tested the half of the fix that was easy to reach'.
guidance_note: When a fix adds the same guard at two sites, write a test for each site before naming the commit, including the one that needs a fixture.

evidence: The F2 fix in 20172c2 records 'every listener is subscribed' via checks.record and then calls mic.say() unconditionally, so a timed-out gate still speaks. 9e16da4 makes it a throwing required() and sweeps the sibling roster check.
guidance_note: When a fix adds a precondition gate, make the code after it unreachable on failure (throw), not just record a FAIL and continue.

evidence: The F10 fix's finally handles leave() rejections via allSettled but leaves `await rooms.call("DeleteRoom", ...)` raw. Because the fix moved DeleteRoom ahead of the reporting loop, a throw there now discards the whole tally. The agent induced a 404 to verify the fix.
guidance_note: When writing a finally block, give every cleanup call in it the same failure treatment, so cleanup errors cannot replace the run's result.

narrative: The original 13 findings were mostly real. The agent judged them well: it pushed back with measurements on DeleteRoom grants and on null rooms, and took better fixes than the ones offered. Seven later findings were the remainders of those fixes: the try/finally left recordSpeech and DeleteRoom unguarded, the subscription gate recorded without gating, guards and modules shipped with half their tests, and comment rewordings missed sibling text. Round 1 consisted entirely of fix-caused findings. Rounds 2 to 4 mixed fix remainders with fresh original-code findings and false positives on the regenerated workflow, which the agent correctly refuted with source checks. The PR hit the 5-round review cap, so the final head commit went unreviewed.
guidance_observations: Every incomplete fix here shared one shape: the agent fixed the instance named, then wrote 'Fixed in' without sweeping for the same assumption in adjacent code (both guard sites, every cleanup call, every 'agent' mention, every exported method).
Self-review before naming a fix commit should reread the fix's own new comments against the code, since two findings (F21, F25) were the fix's comments asserting things the fix did not make true.

A large unrelated generated-workflow regeneration landed mid-review (05d6f5d) and drew five findings across three rounds that had nothing to do with the PR's purpose; landing template churn in its own PR would have saved review scope and helped keep the PR under the round cap.
The agent edited the dotfiles repo from this openconv session to fix F27 at the template source; that is the right fix location but crosses repo scope.
